name: Stephen Fredette
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Steve Fredette is cofounder and president of Toast, which makes restaurant software. He owns 5% of the company.
Toast listed on the New York Stock Exchange in a 2021 IPO that was the largest ever by a Boston-based company.
Fredette and his cofounders, Aman Narang and Jonathan Grimm, attended MIT and worked at Cambridge, Massachusetts-based search software company Endeca together.
The trio launched Toast in 2012 as a mobile payments app for restaurants. The software has expanded to include features for online ordering and delivery.

name: Jiang Zhaobai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2013-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2023); Hurun China (2005-2023)
forbes_bio: Jiang Zhaobai chairs Shanghai Pengxin Group, whose businesses include real estate, financial services and agribusiness.
Jiang founded Shanghai Pengxin Group in 1988.
Jiang graduated from Nanjing Institute of Architecture and Civil Engineering and the China Europe International Business School.

name: Marty Horton
forbes_bio: Marty Horton's late husband Donald Horton (d. 2024) founded homebuilder D.R. Horton in 1978.
She owns a share of the family's more than 10% stake in the business, which is America's largest builder.
D.R. Horton has built more than 1 million homes across 126 markets in 36 states. It did $36.8 billion in fiscal 2024 sales.

name: Gyorgy Gattyan
forbes_bio: Gyorgy Gattyan made the bulk of his fortune from porn site LiveJasmin.com. He is also a cofounder of the International Teqball Federation
He founded the political party Megoldás Mozgalom (Solution Movement) prior the 2022 Hungarian Election but failed to win any seats in Parliament.
He co-founded the Hungarian Prima Primissima Award to celebrate achievements in Hungarian Culture and supports causes related to children in need.
forbes_facts: He is an active movie and TV producer whose work includes the last 11 episodes of the Hungarian Cult-classic animation series, Hungarian Folk Tales.

name: Ruiqing Tan
forbes_bio: Tan Ruiqing is vice chairman of Lomon Billions Group, a supplier of titanium dioxide pigment.
Lomon Billions grew out of a state-owned sulfur-brimstone mine business in Henan Province.

name: Denis Shtengelov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Denis Shtengelov controls KDV, a large food business in Russia that sells everything from candy and beverages to pasta.
Born in the village of Gubino in the Tomsk region, Shtengelov's first business was selling sunflower seeds.
In 1997 Shtengelov bought his first confectionery factory in Yashkino, Kemerovo region with partners.
He also owns retailer Yarche! with 1,400 supermarkets in Russia.
Shtengelov, who has lived in Australia for years, invested $20 million to set up KDV Sport's golf and tennis academy on the country's Gold Coast.
forbes_facts: Shtengelov was an investor in a shopping mall that caught fire in 2018 in a deadly incident that killed  60 people, including 37 children.

name: Gisele Trajano
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021)
forbes_bio: Gisele Trajano is a granddaughter of Luiza Trajano Donato and Pelegrino José Donato, who founded retailer Magazine Luiza in 1957.
Nicknamed "the Amazon of Brazil," Magazine Luiza's e-commerce platforms account for 69% of the company's total revenues.
Along with four other family members who also own shares of Magazine Luiza, Trajano is a new addition to the Forbes Billionaires list in 2021.
